change: Responsive jumps and ledges, safe boat exits and submerged hulls, continuous Scheldt bed and distant-bank scenery.

riverbed.collision: Same surface, double-sided; slopes join the original near-bank mud at z=-80 and the far-bank toe at z=-264. The central channel is approximately 14.5 m below datum; existing shore terrain, stairs and foundations remain.
riverbed.navigation: Water outlines and authored boat placements unchanged. Diver floor queries extend to the new bed.

bank.materials: Existing brick, slate, bluestone, wood, bark, foliage and earth textures; continuous building-space wall/gable UVs, one slate texture span per roof pitch excluding its metal edge strip, world-aligned ground detail, shared fog and daylight shaders.
bank.construction: Terrain-fitted stone foundations, closed gables, overhanging slate roofs, chimneys, window frames and sills, eaves and downpipe outlets at ground level.
bank.edgeExceptions: Buried and mating faces stay flat; slate sheet lips use 2 mm bevels; leaf cards remain thin sheets; the continuous soil surface has no exposed artificial rim within the water bounds.
bank.collision: One static body: one 4,444-triangle bed shape, 136 trunk cylinders and 12 simple convex building shells. Foliage, frames and drainage add no collision shapes. Trunks and crowns are kept clear of the houses.
bank.preservation: Original shore geometry, transforms, IDs and collision retained. Its material is overridden at runtime; new scenery is a separate scene.

rebuild: native-godot/scripts/river-scenery-build.tscn with Forward+ after dotnet build. The dummy renderer cannot serialize tree transforms; the builder rejects it and checks all four buffers before saving.
startup: Serialized assets declared in StartupResources, timed as river.scenery.load, included in the native package content fingerprint. No runtime geometry generation or invalidation of unrelated town/Ruien geometry.
